eeScopeAudit.whyThisWasTheSharpestProbe: D-157's adopted text does not merely assign seven classes — it states in the same passage that three more remain leftover-design. An inventory that silently drops classes its own naming decision says are still open is exactly the defect that produced a blocker on the DR-105 join, so this had to be resolved rather than assumed.
eeScopeAudit.d157Verbatim: 'It owns DR-117 EE-1, EE-2, EE-3b, EE-4, EE-5a, EE-5b, and EE-6a only … Those seven leftover-design close: remainder is G29 execution of both named corpora. EE-7a, EE-7b, and EE-7d remain leftover-design. EE-6b, EE-7c, and EE-7e remain capable-of-riding and unnamed at G09/G14/G16.'
eeScopeAudit.resolution: The three that remain leftover-design are not this gate's. G29 v2 mentions EE-7a, EE-7b and EE-7d in exactly one place — basedOn.g30v1.role, reading 'G30 is useful-install advertisement (EE-7a, EE-7b, EE-7d). Not this gate.' The dispatch forbids taking over G30, so carrying them into this join's inventory would have been the breach. Omitting them is correct. The further three, EE-6b, EE-7c and EE-7e, are placed by D-157 at G09, G14 and G16, likewise not here.

coordinatorSummary: ACCEPT at 0 blockers and 0 SHOULD-FIX. Twenty-two attacks run, none landed. Custody holds: subject 163fd228 at 0444, 10277 bytes, unmoved at both ends; HEAD never left 5d5d778; live required-now 26 of 26; file 08 and COORD unmodified. All five cited pins reproduce, recordedInputs.HEAD equals the top-level head, artifact and version are both 1, and the pinned harness is v2 — the later artifact with its own independent ACCEPT, which is what the dispatch names as live. The token is a condition of acceptance here, so it was measured first: file08StatusToken is the bare string OPEN, the live DR-G29 status cell is OPEN, and no SATISFIED standing has leaked in. The assurance quote equals the live stage cell, and the corpus phrase is a verbatim substring of G29 v2's liveHarnessCellVerbatim, identical in both places the join states it, and matching the corpus segment of the live file 08 harness cell. The substance of this review was one probe. D-157's adopted text does not merely assign seven EE classes to G29 — it says in the same passage that EE-7a, EE-7b and EE-7d remain leftover-design, and that EE-6b, EE-7c and EE-7e remain capable-of-riding at G09, G14 and G16. A join built on that decision which carries none of those six looks, on its face, exactly like the inventory-short defect that produced a blocker on the DR-105 join. It resolved the other way at source: G29 v2 places EE-7a, EE-7b and EE-7d at G30 in terms — 'G30 is useful-install advertisement (EE-7a, EE-7b, EE-7d). Not this gate.' — and the dispatch forbids taking over G30, so carrying them would have been the breach rather than the fix. D-157 itself assigns the seven with the word 'only', and the join's namedClassesThisGate matches element for element. I verified the closure clause 'Those seven leftover-design close: remainder is G29 execution of both named corpora' in the adopted text rather than in the artifact, since that is what lets an obligation sit at leftoverDesign false. Two further checks came back clean: the join cites liveHarnessCellVerbatim and authorityClaim because G29 v2 has no namedCorpusNotAuthored, no namedClassesThisGate and no whatThisCloses — adaptation to the source rather than template-filling, the same property the DR-G27 join showed; and the four gates the dispatch protects appear in exactly one field, a refusal in doesNot. The join also carries the live required-now 26 rather than the 25 D-157 recorded at the time. Bookkeeping reconciles at five and five. Recorded rather than raised: the join is silent on D-056 gates 2 and 3, which is safer here than at its siblings because D-157 states those gates do not hold after that act, so silence contradicts nothing; and the DR-G29 harness cell still reads 'not authored' while G29 v2 exists — the ninth row in that condition, covered by my standing recommendation that the coordinator dispose of the family in one act.
